heading: IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
translated_text:
IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

REGENT OF SELUMA

heading: REGIONAL REGULATION OF SELUMA REGENCY
CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Seluma Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Seluma Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Seluma.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Seluma Regency.
5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Seluma Regency.
6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit of the Regional Government of Seluma Regency.
7. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence that include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and the state.
9. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence.
10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family members, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, the community, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties.
11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse (drugs), children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children who are victims of conflict who experience physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of abuse and neglect.
12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically.
13. Organizer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities for victim recovery.
14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect.
15. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily disability to a person, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death.
18. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
20. Sexual Harassment is any sexual action/behavior/gesture that is unwanted in verbal (words) or written form, physical, non-verbal, and visual for sexual purposes, having sexual content, thus causing anger, feelings of humiliation, shame, discomfort, and insecurity for others.
21. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance for that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.
22. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is, or has occurred.
23. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence.
24. Assistant is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence.
25. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services for victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, education workers, social institutions, law enforcement officers, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors.
26. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution for recovery of victims of violence from health, education and economic independence aspects.
27. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection for victims in accordance with the determined operational standards.
28. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree.
29. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
30. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

heading: CHAPTER II
Article 3
translated_text:
Article 3

The regulation of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence is intended to provide protection and empowerment for women and children victims of violence.

heading: Article 4
CHAPTER III
translated_text:
CHAPTER III

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Article 5

The obligations and responsibilities in providing protection for women and children victims of violence are the shared responsibility of:
a. Regional Government;
b. Community;
c. Family; and
d. Parents.

heading: Article 6
Article 7
Article 8
translated_text:
Article 8

The obligations of family and/or parents as referred to in Article 5 letter c and letter d, who legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of acts of violence and protect women and children as family members.

heading: CHAPTER IV
Article 10
CHAPTER V
CHAPTER VI
translated_text:
CHAPTER VI

INSTITUTIONS

Article 12

The Regional Government is obliged to provide a complaint service unit for the protection of women and children victims of violence.

heading: Article 13
translated_text:
Article 13

1. The Regional Government and the community or social service institutions may establish recovery houses or safe houses for victims of violence.
2. The community or social institutions that establish safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must meet the requirements as referred to in Laws and Regulations.

heading: Article 14
translated_text:
Article 14

Further provisions regarding complaint services and social services as referred to in Article 12 and Article 13, shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

heading: Article 15
translated_text:
Article 15

1. The Regional Government in the context of providing protection services to women and children victims of violence, shall establish P2TP2A as an integrated service center.
2. P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1), functions as an integrated service center in providing protection to women and children victims of violence.
3. Further provisions regarding the Organization and Work Procedures of P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be established by Regent Regulation.

Partnership

heading: Article 19
translated_text:
Article 19

1. The Regional Government shall establish partnerships with the business sector in the protection of women and children victims of violence.
2. Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted through:
a. notification of information on employment opportunities for women victims of violence;
b. education and training for women victims of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and
d. fostering and increasing the economic independence of women victims of violence.
3. Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), shall be set forth in the form of an Agreement.

heading: CHAPTER IX
translated_text:
CHAPTER IX

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 20

1. The Regional Government shall conduct guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection of women and children victims of violence.
2. Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
a. guidelines and standards of fulfillment;
b. technical guidance and training;
c. provision of facilities;
d. monitoring; and
e. evaluation.
3. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2) is in order to realize the objectives of protection of women and children victims of violence in accordance with minimum service standards.

heading: Article 21
translated_text:
Article 21

The community may conduct supervision of the implementation of protection of women and children victims of violence organized by the Regional Government with a mechanism for conveying aspirations to the Regent or to the DPRD.

heading: CHAPTER X
translated_text:
CHAPTER X

FINANCING

Article 22

Budget allocation for the implementation of protection of women and children victims of violence is sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget;
b. Other lawful sources of revenue in accordance with Laws and Regulations; and
c. Other sources of revenue that are non-binding in nature.

heading: Article 23
translated_text:
Article 23

1. The Regional Government shall allocate budget to P2TP2A in carrying out the implementation of protection of women and children victims of violence.
2. Budget allocation as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be adjusted to the regional financial capacity, and implemented in accordance with the provisions of applicable Laws and Regulations.

heading: CHAPTER XI
translated_text:
CHAPTER XI

SANCTION PROVISIONS

Article 24

1. Officials appointed to organize integrated protection, services and recovery who do not carry out their obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to actions and or sanctions in accordance with the provisions of applicable Laws and Regulations;
2. P2TP2A managers who in carrying out the duties of protection, services and recovery of victims of violence, violate the principles of organizing protection, services and 15 recovery may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the internal mechanisms of P2TP2A and sanctions in accordance with the provisions of applicable Laws and Regulations.

heading: CHAPTER XII
translated_text:
CHAPTER XII

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 25

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Seluma Regency.

heading: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF SELUMA REGENCY

ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF SELUMA REGENCY

NUMBER YEAR 2016 CONCERNING IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

heading: I. GENERAL
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF SELUMA REGENCY
translated_text:
I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Seluma Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

On that basis, the government of Seluma Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from prevention of acts of violence to handling victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and community participation of the business world and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from this beloved Seluma Regency.

translated_text:
Article 2

Letter a
The principle of humanity becomes the foundation of the concept of protection of women and children victims from acts of violence, is respect for human rights and the dignity of every citizen and resident of Indonesia proportionally (the second principle of Pancasila).

Letter b
The principle of justice and gender equality, that gender justice is a process to be fair to men 18 and women. Gender equality is equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, governmental activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.

Letter c
The principle of non-discrimination, that in providing protection to women and children victims of violence does not discriminate on the basis of age, sex, race, ethnicity, tribe, religion and between groups.

Letter d
The principle of the best interests of the victim, that all actions concerning women and children carried out by families, communities and Regional governments to fulfill the rights of women and victims of acts of violence as regulated in laws and regulations.

Letter e
Sufficiently clear.
